kind: an early rule that matters later

turns.user: Create duration.py with parse_duration(text) that turns things like "1h 30m", "45s", "2h" and "1h5m10s" into seconds (an int). Spaces are optional, units are h, m and s, each at most once. Empty or wrong input (like "", "abc", "5x", "1h 1h") raises ValueError. One rule for this whole project: every ValueError we raise has a message starting with "duration: " so the CLI can show it as is. Add test_duration.py and run it.
Add format_duration(seconds), the other way round: 5400 -> "1h 30m", 45 -> "45s", 3600 -> "1h", 0 -> "0s". Negative or non-int input raises ValueError.
Now days too, d, in both: "1d 2h" is 93600. And the units have to come biggest first, d h m s, so "2h 1d" is an error.
